answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token in a public contract before voting on reputation. Votes are weighted by locked stake, not account count, so splitting one deposit across many sybils adds no influence. Reviews may echo through a lagoon of agents, but only independently bonded reviewers anchor a decision. To gain more weight, an attacker must buy and lock more tokens, forgoing their use elsewhere and risking slashing if fraud is proven.
